title: kernel-sprint-scratch-luca
summary: Morning scratchpad for kernel + kv-cache triage. Short reproducer, immediate TODOs, experiments to run after standup.
body:
Morning checklist
- coffee: yes
- quick triage window: 30m before standup
- main focus: intermittent double-free seen in kv-cache when prefix eviction triggers during concurrent prefix writes

Observed behavior
- % of requests: ~0.05% (seen in prod sampling)
- symptom: worker OOM then SIGSEGV; dmesg shows free on already-freed pointer in kv_cache.c:evict_prefix
- repro attempts: flaky in CI; deterministic when running concurrency=64 synthetic workload w/ short prefixes + forced eviction interval=50ms

Quick repro steps (local)
1) checkout branch: runtime/fix/kv-eject-debug (locally patch to enable heavy-logging)
2) build with ASAN: make -j8 CFLAGS='-fsanitize=address -g'
3) run repro: ./kv_repro --concurrency 64 --prefixes 2000 --evict-ms 50 --seed 42
4) if it crashes: collect core, addr2line on symbols, attach to GH issue

Immediate hypotheses (ranked)
- race between eviction and write path: write increments refcount but eviction path can win if sequence of events aligns (most likely)
- stale pointer from freelist reuse due to missing memory barrier in producers
- delayed GC callback invoked twice for same entry (less likely but possible with timer reschedule bug)

Quick checks to add to CI
- add 'thread_fuzzer' build config to CI job (RT-kv-threads) and run for 2k iterations on PRs touching kv-cache
- enable per-entry epoch stamps to assert monotonicity (cheap assert, to catch early)

Perf TODOs (not blockers for triage but important next)
- measure tail latency delta when we enable epoch assertions: run 24h perf harness with p95/p99 breakdown
- experiment: reduce continuous-batching threshold from 16->12 to see impact on 1-token tail under high contention (baseline: 16)
- run int8-quantized model serving with kv-cache warmup disabled to measure effect on first-request latency (script: perf/run_quant_experiments.sh)

Notes for kernel-level debugging
- suspected ordering issue in evict_prefix: check memory_order_release on write path and memory_order_acquire in evict path for refcount ops
- add tracepoints: kv_cache:entry_alloc, entry_inc_ref, entry_dec_ref, entry_free -> correlate with flame graphs of 1s windows around crash
- candidate fix: switch freelist to hazard-pointer-like pattern or add per-thread deferred-free queue drained by GC thread

Action items (today)
- [ ] create minimal GH PR with ASAN repro and extra asserts (assign to @Diego)
- [ ] run long-thread-fuzz job in CI (me)
- [ ] pair with Priya to review eviction timer reschedule logic (30m after standup)
- [ ] write brief note to SRE on increasing core dump retention for debug machines (cc: eng-sre)

Housekeeping notes
- bump issue priority if repro hits 3x in 24h sampling window
- flag for release: hold rollout of runtime v1.23.0 to low-risk pool until we confirm fix

Brain-dump: alternate perf idea
- adaptive batch window: instead of fixed ms window, use a tiny ML model (logistic reg) that predicts whether to flush current batch based on features: current queue length, observed mean latency last 100ms, avg token size. Train on past 2 weeks of serving traces. Could be overkill but worth A/B as an experiment in Optimize.

Random quick notes (for later)
- Priya found a weird gcc 12 optimization that changed alignment on x86_64; keep note to try -fno-strict-aliasing if we trace strange pointer aliasing
- Diego: check your local /etc/sysctl.conf for vm.max_map_count when running large-memory repros

End-of-day followups planned
- collate ASAN logs and file a single artifact in GH issue (link to artifact storage)
- quick write-up for team retro: what tripped us and how to prevent similar regressions

Scratchpad dump ends.
notes: Informal scratch — patching steps and triage checklist. Not ready for doc publishing.
